title: Supporting context for translation performance
prose: What supporting context — beyond the bare term — maximises EN->KO translation quality? Candidates from SNOMED itself: the semantic tag (always present, cheap disambiguation), the parent / is-a hierarchy (sense + domain), synonyms, and text definitions (rich but only ~2.4% of concepts). Plus the existing levers: retrieval exemplars and the style guide. This is the TRANSLATION-PERFORMANCE arm of the project — reduce errors at the source — distinct from the confidence thread (output-translations-confidence), which PRIORITISES review of what remains. Both serve the root goal of minimising terminologist effort, and they interact: better context lowers the error rate, and some context (e.g. detected ambiguity) may itself feed a confidence signal.

notes.body:
**Adding SNOMED concept context to the EN->KO prompt is neutral overall but helps the ambiguous tail — and ONLY if the context is fenced off.** Translated 960 concepts (120 each across 8 hierarchies, gemma4-26b-qat) under three prompts — bare / +semantic-tag / +parent hierarchy — scored vs the KR gold (multi-reference chrF + BGE semantic).

- First, a trap: naively appending '(organism)'/parent lists LEAKED into the output (땅콩(균) and HURT quality (chrF 58.0 -> 54.0). Fencing the context with explicit 'context only, do NOT include' labels fixed the leak (5/960 artifacts).
- Fenced, context is ~neutral overall: bare 58.0 / +tag 58.0 / +parents **58.5** chrF (sem ~0.82 flat).
- But it helps SELECTIVELY on ambiguous hierarchies: organism +2.8 chrF (53.2->56.0), qualifier value +3.5 (59.4->62.9); flat/slightly negative on concrete types (disorder, procedure, substance) the model already nails.

Caveats: deltas are modest and n=120/hierarchy (noisy); chrF/sem-to-gold penalises valid alternative translations, so it may UNDERSTATE context value for precision — an SME spot-check on the ambiguous tail is the real test. Text definitions (only ~2.4% of concepts) untested as a sub-condition.

Implication for prompt optimisation: don't blanket-add context — add it CONDITIONALLY for ambiguous/rare concept types, and the format must clearly separate context from the term. This is the signal to feed GEPA: let the optimiser learn WHEN to pull which context. Reproduced by scripts/analysis/concept_context_translation.py (scripted, not yet a flow node).
notes.author: research-agent

notes.body:
**The reference metric WAS masking a jump — a blind judge shows context wins ~2:1 on the ambiguous tail.** chrF/semantic-to-gold penalise a valid-but-divergent translation, so I re-tested the 251 cases where +parents changed the output with a blind pairwise LLM judge (shown the English concept + context, NOT the gold; A/B order randomised).

- Overall (changed cases): +parents 52% vs bare 45% — modest, ~ what the metric implied.
- But on the genuinely AMBIGUOUS types the judge reveals a strong win the metric hid: **organism +parents 69% vs 31%** (metric showed only +2.8 chrF), **qualifier value 66% vs 34%** (+3.5 chrF), finding 57% vs 38%.
- And context genuinely HURTS the concrete types (not a metric artifact): **body structure bare 71% vs 26%**, disorder bare 56%.

So the earlier 'neutral' read was a mean over a harsh metric: parent context gives a real ~2:1 quality lift where the bare term is ambiguous (organisms need taxonomic context; qualifier values like 'Left'/'Severe' are meaningless alone), and a real loss where it isn't. Caveats: judge is gemma4 (same model as translator) — blind pairwise between its own two outputs mitigates but doesn't remove self-bias; a stronger/SME judge would confirm; n per hierarchy on changed cases is ~30 (directional). 

Actionable policy for prompt optimisation: add parent context CONDITIONALLY — yes for organism / qualifier value / finding, NO for body structure / disorder. Reproduced by scripts/analysis/concept_context_judge.py.
notes.author: research-agent

notes.body: Leakage audit for fable_gepa_judge_v1 (and the shared eval setup): checked whether the pooled_legacy exemplar corpus (data/EN-KO/all_bilingual_pairs.csv — 363,812 unique English terms / 475,700 EN→KO pairs) hands the canonical gold to the model during translation. Result: NO gold leakage. Exact-English overlap with the held-out sets is 0/124 test, 0/125 dev, 7/625 train (1.1%); exact (English, gold-Korean) pairs present in the pool = 0 across ALL splits. Retrieval (lookup_pairs) has no self-exclusion filter but doesn't need one — the query terms aren't in the pool. Verified on the GEPA lookup_cache that dev/test exemplars are related-but-different SNOMED concepts (e.g. "MR arthrography of upper limb without contrast" retrieves "CT of upper limb without contrast" — same frame, different modality), never the answer; 0/24 keyed dev+test terms had their own EN or gold-KO among exemplars. Corroborated by the seed baseline scoring only 28% (would be ~100% if the gold were retrieved). Conclusion: GEPA training and the 55.6%-test eval are fair, apples-to-apples with the hand-guide 58.1% baseline (identical exemplar setup for all guides).
notes.author: agent

notes.body: CORRECTION to note-1 (which is WRONG). note-1 claimed "no gold leakage" based on exact-English matching, but that was defeated by FSN semantic tags: the pool English is "... (procedure)" while the splits use bare preferred_term, so exact-EN match spuriously returned 0%. The truth: the pooled_legacy corpus (all_bilingual_pairs.csv) INCLUDES the Korean SNOMED extension (39,056 'SNOMED' + 17,722 'SNOMED_synonyms' pairs), and the dspy_splits ARE extension procedure concepts — so their gold Korean is in the pool. Rigorous check (tag-stripped EN + Korean-side): 85.5% of test terms have their exact concept->gold-KO in the pool. DECISIVE: in the exemplar cache the eval actually fed the model (lookup_cache.exemplars_pooled_legacy_ko_1aca69d6.json), 109/124 = 87.9% of test terms had their gold Korean among the retrieved exemplars (e.g. query 'Ultrasonography of oral cavity' -> exemplar 'Ultrasonography of oral cavity (procedure)' -> 구강 초음파 검사 = the gold). So the held-out TEST numbers (GEPA+Fable 55.6%, hand v5_1 58.1%, induced ~50%) are INFLATED by ~88% gold-in-exemplar leakage and measure exemplar-selection, not from-scratch translation. Nuance that rescues the core finding: the GEPA run + its internal dev-50 metric used a DIFFERENT cache (data/sme_review/2026-04-24/lookup_cache.json), which has 0% gold leak and where a cache-miss yields NO exemplars (_format_exemplars: lookup_cache.get(sctid) or []). So the GEPA dev improvement 28%->42% exact is CLEAN (gold-free) and IS trustworthy evidence that Fable's feedback improves translation. But note the train/eval regime mismatch (GEPA trained gold-free, tested gold-leaked). Recommend a clean re-eval: self-concept-exclusion at retrieval, or evaluate on the ~100 extension-EXTERNAL SME terms whose golds are not in the pool.
notes.author: agent
